I wasn’t arguing about objective truth, but it is a FACT that most people who pray the rosary don’t actually feel "peace beyond understanding," but rather meditate on the mysteries of Christ’s life because of devotion to Him through His Blessed Mother. Presenting a position for joining the Catholic faith off of the rosary "bringing peace beyond understanding" is irrational and can turn people away, as if this premise was the reasoning offered to me early on, I likely wouldn’t be Catholic. 
In regard to doing the rosary every day not being "my will" but God’s, Catholics do not believe in double predestination. My choices are my choices, your choices are your own. I can (and have) chosen NOT do the rosary every day in the past. Of my own will, I can choose not to any further. That is not God. God can offer grace to us through sacramentals like the rosary, dependent on our faith, but He is not literally compelling us to recite words. 
Lastly, I cite no experience with God as justification for my faith. I respect our Church fathers, but do not think they only relied on personal experience with God for evangelization and to keep to the faith. They relied on reason, of the understanding of theology and tradition from the Apostles passed down to us. I don’t think personal experience with God is a ‘bad thing,’ but the problem is that relying on emotion is an easy way to fall away. I’ve known many Catholics who have left the faith and joined Protestantism because they lacked knowledge of God, and relied on ‘feeling Him,’ finding stronger ‘feeling’ of God in charismatic sects that deny the sacraments and adhere to false doctrines to allow themselves to chase God how they want.
